facts.statement: Animantarx was a slow-moving, four-legged herbivore covered in heavy armor but lacked a tail club.
facts.quote: Like other nodosaurs, it would have been a slow-moving quadrupedal herbivore covered in heavy armor scutes, but without a tail club.

facts.statement: Animantarx had a skull about 25 cm long and a total body length of no more than 3 meters.
facts.quote: The skull measures approximately 25 cm (10 inches) in length, suggesting the animal as a whole was no more than 3 meters (10 feet) long.

facts.statement: Only a single specimen of Animantarx has been discovered to date.
facts.quote: Only one specimen of Animantarx has so far been recovered.

facts.statement: Animantarx was the first dinosaur discovered using a radioactivity detection method.
facts.quote: Este dinosaurio acorazado fue el primero en ser encontrado mediante el método de detección de radioactividad.

facts.statement: The species is named after Ramal Jones, who found the specimen using a modified Geiger counter in an area with no exposed bones.
facts.quote: La especie se nombra por Ramal Jones, que descubrió el espécimen usando un centellometro modificado en un área sin huesos expuestos.

facts.statement: Animantarx lived during the Late Cretaceous, approximately 106 to 97 million years ago.
facts.quote: This section of the formation is believed to represent the late Albian through early Cenomanian stages of the Late Cretaceous Period, or about 106 to 97 million years ago.

facts.statement: Fossils found in mudstone alongside aquatic animals suggest Animantarx lived in a floodplain environment.
facts.quote: The presence of aquatic animals like fish and frogs, as well as the mudstone in which their fossils are found, suggests that this was a floodplain environment.

facts.statement: Animantarx lived in what is now North America during the Cenomanian and Turonian stages, roughly 98 to 90 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 98 y 90 millones de años, en el Cenomaniense y Turoniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Animantarx is classified as a nodosaurid ankylosaur, though its exact position within the family remains uncertain.
facts.quote: Animantarx is universally thought of as a nodosaurid ankylosaur, although its precise relationships within that family are uncertain.

facts.statement: Animantarx belongs to the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Recent analyses exclude Animantarx from the main ankylosaur tree, classifying it as Nodosauridae incertae sedis due to unique skull and shoulder features.
facts.quote: The most recent cladistic analysis of ankylosaur phylogeny does not include Animantarx, although the authors recognize the genus as Nodosauridae incertae sedis because of its rounded supraorbital protrusions and a "knoblike" acromion on the scapula.

facts.statement: Some studies suggest Animantarx is the closest relative of Edmontonia within the Nodosauridae family.
facts.quote: Two separate studies have found Animantarx to be the sister taxon of Edmontonia within Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: The name Animantarx means "living citadel" in Latin, referencing the animal's armored nature.
facts.quote: The generic name is composed of the Latin words animatus ("living" or "animated") and arx ("fortress" or "citadel"), referring to its armored nature.

facts.statement: The name honors paleontologist R.S. Lull's description of ankylosaurs as "living citadels" that were practically unassailable.
facts.quote: El nombre se basa en la observación con respecto a los anquilosaurianos, que hiciese Richard Swann Lull donde los describe como "ciudadelas vivientes, estos animales deben haber sido prácticamente inatacables...".

facts.statement: Animantarx is classified as a member of the Ankylosauria order within the family Nodosauridae, though its exact relationships within that family remain uncertain.
facts.quote: Animantarx es considerado en como un Ankylosauria de la familia Nodosauridae, aunque sus lazos exactos dentro de esa familia son inciertos.

facts.statement: Recent cladistic analyses of ankylosaurian phylogeny do not include Animantarx, leading researchers to classify the genus as incertae sedis within Nodosauridae based on its rounded supraorbital protuberances and a handle-shaped acromion on the scapula.
facts.quote: El análisis cladístico más reciente de la filogenia de los ankylosaurianos no incluye Animantarx, aunque los autores reconocen el género como incertae sedis de Nodosauridae debido a sus protuberancias supraorbital redondeadas y un acromion con forma de manija en la escápula.

facts.statement: Two separate studies have found that Animantarx is the closest relative of Edmontonia within the family Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Dos estudios separados ha encontrado que Animantarx es el pariente más cercano de Edmontonia dentro de Nodosauridae.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Animantarx is Nodosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Nodosauridae

facts.statement: Animantarx belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Animantarx lived during the Aptian to Albian stages, approximately 121.4 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (121.4 to 100.5 million years ago)
